🇬🇧 The empire on which the sun never set — every country British forces reached, 1169 → 1957.

Britain is less than 0.2% of the world's land, yet its forces reached 94 of today's countries ⚓ The key was the Royal Navy: for centuries it carried settlers, redcoats and gunboats across every ocean, and after Trafalgar in 1805 no fleet could challenge it for a hundred years. One surprise on the map: after World War One, Cecil Rhodes' dream of an unbroken British line "from Cairo to Cape Town" actually came true 🗺️

Was yours one of them? 👇

📊 Data: S. Laycock, All the Countries We've Ever Invaded; Wikipedia — wars involving the United Kingdom. Laycock's broader count reaches 171; this map only keeps colonies, land invasions and direct attacks (raid, naval, blockade). Present-day borders, microstates not drawn.
